title: Build Your First AI App in Under 10 Minutes
angle: Most people think building AI apps requires years of coding — this scenario destroys that myth by showing a complete beginner shipping a real AI app faster than watching a Netflix episode.

scenes.voiceover: I built a working AI app in 7 minutes. No coding degree. No bootcamp. Watch.
scenes.visual_description: Extreme close-up of shocked face staring at screen, then whip-pan to timer showing 7:00 counting down on a bright screen.
scenes.caption_overlay: 7 MINUTES. REAL AI APP. NO BS.

scenes.scene_name: The Setup — Anyone Can Do This
scenes.voiceover: All you need is a browser and a free account. That's it. No installs. No terminal. Nothing scary.
scenes.visual_description: Rapid zoom into browser URL bar, typing a URL, free signup form appearing — all in fast-cut motion with bold text highlights.

scenes.voiceover: Drag. Drop. Connect the AI block. Type your prompt. Done. Your app just got a brain.
scenes.visual_description: Hyperspeed screen recording — UI blocks snapping together, AI node lighting up in neon blue, prompt field filling with text, output appearing instantly.

scenes.voiceover: I typed a question. It answered. In real time. This is a live AI app I built in under 10 minutes.
scenes.visual_description: Split screen: developer's amazed face on the left, AI app responding on the right — response text animates in word by word with a glowing border.

scenes.scene_name: The Stakes — Why You Can't Wait
scenes.voiceover: People are launching AI startups with this. Right now. While you're still watching.
scenes.visual_description: Black screen with white bold text slamming in word by word — STARTUPS. LAUNCHED. TODAY. — then a rapid fire montage of app screenshots flashing at 12fps.

scenes.voiceover: Link in bio. Free. Takes 7 minutes. Come back and tell me I'm wrong.
scenes.visual_description: Speaker holds up phone showing the finished app, then smirks directly into camera — same extreme close-up framing as scene one, completing the visual loop.

hook_test.format_reference: Wait, what? — Hook with surprising claim → proof → bigger reveal
hook_test.viral_proof: Videos using the 'impossible speed claim + live proof' format consistently hit 10M+ views. Reference: Fireship's '100 seconds of code' series (YouTube, 50M+ total views), TikTok dev creators like @indiecoder showing 'built in X minutes' formats averaging 8-15M views per clip in 2023-2024.
hook_test.why_it_works: The timer creates involuntary tension — viewers stay to see if the claim is real. The beginner-friendly angle removes the 'not for me' scroll trigger. The live screen recording adds credibility that defeats skepticism mid-watch.
